name: leo_1day_jgm2_8x8_sunmoon_srp

propagator_readback.note: read from prop.GetPropagator() after PrepareInternals(), not the front-end Propagator or the bare integrator object -- see gen_leo_1day_jgm2_8x8.py's module doc

reason: N3's SRP arc: the leo_1day_jgm2_8x8_sunmoon arc with spherical SolarRadiationPressure added and no drag, so SRP is the only force added relative to a golden that already exists and the whole-day residual is attributable to it alone. The arc was chosen partly because it passes through Earth's shadow (this file's own shadow_summary records 37.0 percent of the day in umbra and 0.28 percent in penumbra by this crate's own shadow function), so the golden exercises the shadow model and not only the sunlit cannonball term. TOLERANCE: measured first, then recorded. crates/av-orbital/tests/srp_goldens.rs::trajectory_residual_against_golden_b measured 3.168026e-3 m / 3.549427e-6 m/s for the native Dopri5 model against this file's GMAT PrinceDormand78 end state (debug build, cargo test -p av-orbital --test srp_goldens -- --nocapture --test-threads=1, GMAT R2026a in-process). 4e-3 m is that residual with a 1.26x margin, the same order and the same shape of margin leo_1day_jgm2_8x8_mars_jupiter.json records over its own measurement. The previous revision of this file carried a 100 m placeholder tolerance from the first pass of that measure-then-record loop; a 100 m tolerance on a 500 km LEO arc pins nothing, which is round 1's own recorded review lesson, and this regeneration closes the loop.

shadow_summary.note: computed by this script's own illumination_fraction (a Python port of crates/av-orbital/src/srp.rs, itself a port of GMAT's ShadowState::FindShadowState/GetPercentSunInPenumbra), applied to a SEPARATE, finer (MaxStep=60s) propagation of the same initial state/gravity model, sampling GMAT's own reported spacecraft position and Sun position (via CoordinateConverter) every 60 s -- NOT GMAT's own SolarRadiationPressure.PercentSun, which this file's own module doc explains cannot be read back this way (it reflects an internal clone PrepareInternals() builds, not the configured object this script holds a handle to). Never touches x0/final_state above.
